tcd-nursing-midwifery-international-scho.about:
Trinity College Dublin's School of Nursing & Midwifery runs a two-week International Winter School (4–15 January 2027) and Summer School (17–28 May 2027). The programme combines learning about Irish healthcare and clinical practice with Irish culture, including a tour of Trinity and the Book of Kells and a Celtic Nights dinner and show. It earns 5 ECTS and a certificate of completion.

It is aimed at (groups of) undergraduate nursing and midwifery students from higher-education institutions, who must complete occupational-health screening, a police background check and immunity blood tests.

The fee is €1,615. Applications are handled in order received by email to snmglobal@tcd.ie; full payment secures a place.
highlights: Ireland's top university
5 ECTS for nursing/midwifery students
Book of Kells and cultural programme
tcd-nursing-midwifery-international-scho.eligibility: Undergraduate nursing and midwifery students (usually in groups from their university); health screening, police clearance and vaccination blood tests required.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 prospectus on the TCD page.
Email snmglobal@tcd.ie to apply (individually or via your university).
Complete health screening and police clearance.
Pay the €1,615 fee in full to secure your place.
tcd-nursing-midwifery-international-scho.costs: €1,615 (tuition, Trinity tour, Book of Kells, Celtic Nights dinner and show). Accommodation, travel and food not included.

techgirls-2027.about:
TechGirls is a US government-sponsored programme that brings teenage girls interested in technology to the United States. Participants spend 23 days in the US: an intensive tech camp with a partner university (coding, robotics, design), visits to tech companies, and a community-immersion period with host families in one of six US cities. Afterwards each participant leads a community project at home with seven months of mentorship.

Girls aged 15–17 are competitively selected from the US and from listed countries, including Cameroon, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, Zambia, Algeria, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia, Jordan, Lebanon, Argentina, Brazil, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, Suriname, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan and others. The programme is fully funded; the eligible-country list can change each year, so check the 2027 call.
highlights: Fully funded trip to the USA
University tech camp plus host-community stay
Seven months of mentorship for a home project
techgirls-2027.eligibility: Girls aged 15–17, citizens and residents of the participating countries listed for the cycle (2026 list includes Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia, Argentina, Brazil, Peru and others), with English proficiency and interest in STEM.
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 eligible-country list on techgirlsglobal.org
Complete the online application when the call opens (usually winter)
Write essays on your STEM interest and leadership
Attend an interview if shortlisted
Obtain parental consent and a US J-1 visa (sponsored)
techgirls-2027.costs: Fully funded: international travel, accommodation, meals, programme activities and visa sponsorship.

techmun-xxxiv-tjhsst-2027.about:
TechMUN is the long-running conference of the Model UN club at Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology in Northern Virginia, one of the top public high schools in the US; 2027 is its 34th session.

The conference runs 2–3 April 2027 at Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology (TJHSST), Alexandria, United States. It is open to middle and high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Priority registration opens in early November 2026 on the official TJMUN site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 2–3 April 2027 in Alexandria, United States
34th session at a top US STEM high school
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
techmun-xxxiv-tjhsst-2027.eligibility: Open to middle and high school students and school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Priority registration opens in early November 2026 on the official TJMUN site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
techmun-xxxiv-tjhsst-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

teknofest-agricultural-technologies-2027.about:
TEKNOFEST is Türkiye's aviation, space and technology festival, organised by the Turkish Technology Team Foundation (T3 Vakfı) with the Ministry of Industry and Technology. Its competitions run for several months through reports, presentations and qualification stages, ending with finals at the festival. This competition is open to teams studying in Türkiye and abroad, so students from the Caucasus, Central Asia and elsewhere can enter.

Teams submit a project preliminary assessment form, a semi-final presentation and a prototype with final presentation, with separate levels for school students and for university and above.

In the 2026 cycle applications closed on 15 March 2026; the 2027 specification and calendar will be published on the competition page, and applications are made online through the TEKNOFEST portal. Finalists receive official digital certificates from the Ministry of Industry and Technology, training and Q&A sessions, technical tours, internship opportunities and, at university level, access to the TEKNOFEST Startup Program. 2026 prizes up to TRY 100,000 (university level).
highlights: Smart-farming and agritech prototypes
Open to teams studying abroad, free to enter
Certificates, technical tours, internships and prize money for finalists
teknofest-agricultural-technologies-2027.eligibility: Students (school level and university level, including master's, doctorate and open education), graduates and startups studying or based in Türkiye or abroad, at the level defined in the specification.
how_to_apply: Open the competition page on teknofest.org and read the 2027 specification when it is published.
Form a team (with an advisor where required).
Apply online through the TEKNOFEST portal before the 2027 deadline.
Submit the required reports and pass the evaluation stages.
Compete in the finals at TEKNOFEST 2027 if selected.
teknofest-agricultural-technologies-2027.costs: No application fee. Teams fund their own projects; finalists may get material and travel support under TEKNOFEST support programmes. 2026 prizes up to TRY 100,000 (university level).

tu-berlin-winter-school-2027.about:
TU Berlin's Winter School 2027 offers intensive, interactive English-taught courses in areas such as Python programming, entrepreneurship and space science. Four-week courses run 5–29 January 2027, two-week courses 5–15 January and a three-week course 5–22 January; an online term runs 4–29 January.

Participants receive a TU Berlin certificate and can earn up to 6 ECTS, with a cultural programme in Berlin. It is open to students, graduates and working professionals.

Registration is open; check fees, requirements and scholarships on the TU Berlin summer/winter school pages.

Up to 6 ECTS
On-campus or online term

tuba-summer-school-turkology-art-civiliz.about:
The Traditional Summer School on Turkology, Art and the History of Civilization is organised by the Turkish Academy of Sciences (TÜBA), the International Turkic Academy (Astana) and Selçuk University. The 8th edition ran on 23-30 August 2026 at Selçuk University in Konya; a 9th edition is expected in summer 2027.

It brings together young scholars from Turkic-speaking and partner countries for lectures and seminars on relations within the Turkic world, the history of Turkic states, archaeology, art history and Turkic languages and literatures, plus skills sessions on publishing, presenting and winning research grants. Teaching is in Turkish, and up to 35 participants receive a certificate.
highlights: Free flight, meals and accommodation
Lectures by leading scholars from Turkic states
Seljuk heritage in Konya
tuba-summer-school-turkology-art-civiliz.eligibility: In 2026: citizens of Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Northern Cyprus, North Macedonia, Kosovo, Albania, Montenegro, Mongolia, Uzbekistan, Türkiye, Turkmenistan and Jordan who are doctoral students or postdoctoral researchers, with good Turkish. Check the 2027 country list.

Prepare passport copy, highest diploma (and PhD student certificate), a 250-300-word statement of purpose and one signed recommendation letter.
Apply online through summerschool.tuba.gov.tr before the deadline.
Results are announced by email and on the TÜBA website (July in 2026).
tuba-summer-school-turkology-art-civiliz.costs: Fully funded: return flight, meals and accommodation covered by the organisers. No-shows are charged the ticket cost.

tuj-high-school-summer-program-2027.about:
Temple University, Japan Campus (TUJ), the oldest foreign university in Japan, runs an eight-night summer programme in Tokyo for high-school students, from 28 July to 5 August 2027. Students take Japanese language classes (beginner to advanced, no prior Japanese needed) and electives in art, international affairs, international business, film, e-sports or tourism and event management.

The programme includes an overnight trip to Nikko, a day at Tokyo DisneySea, and joint events and meals with Japanese high-school students, with TUJ staff and students supporting participants throughout.

It is open to students entering grades 9–12 in 2027–28. Applications open in late fall 2026; the first 20 accepted students who pay by 1 February 2027 get ¥20,000 off.

Japanese language plus electives
Meet Japanese high-school students

ualberta-global-changemakers-summer-2027.about:
Global Changemakers: Leadership, Diplomacy and Global Challenges is the University of Alberta's 2027 International Summer Program, designed for international undergraduate students. Over four weeks in Edmonton, participants take part in interactive workshops, team-based learning and an immersive global-challenge simulation, attend Indigenous learning sessions, visit the Alberta Legislature and volunteer in the local community.

The CAD 4,000 fee includes 27 nights of accommodation, weekday lunches, all workshops and activities, excursions including the Rocky Mountains, materials and on-campus support. Applicants who apply by 31 December 2026 get CAD 100 off; the final deadline is 15 February 2027. Flights, visa costs, insurance and other meals are extra.

uam-summer-school-economics-business-202.about:
The UAM Summer School of Economics and Business (SSEB) is a four-week programme in Madrid, 28 June – 23 July 2027, taught in English by UAM's Faculty of Economics and Business. Courses include Climate Change Economics, Financial Management in Multinational Firms, Global Marketing and Business Negotiation; each is worth 6 ECTS. A two-week option (28 June – 9 July) is also possible.

Tuition includes social and cultural events and field trips. You can combine the first two weeks with UAM's Tourism Summer School or the SpaCIE Climate Change Summer School.

Early-bird applications (12.5% off) run until 15 February 2027; standard applications until 4 June 2027.

Field trips and cultural events included
12.5% early-bird + 12.5% partner discounts

uam-tourism-summer-school-2027.about:
UAM's Tourism Summer School runs 12–23 July 2027 at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid. It focuses on tourism economics, destination management and Spain as one of the world's leading tourism markets, taught in English by UAM faculty.

Students who attend it can also enrol in the first two weeks of the Summer School of Economics and Business (28 June – 9 July) for a full month in Madrid.

Early-bird applications run until 15 February 2027, standard applications until 18 June 2027.

uba-spanish-for-foreigners-2027.about:
The Laboratorio de Idiomas of the University of Buenos Aires (UBA) Faculty of Philosophy and Letters teaches Spanish to foreigners year-round. Learners take level courses from introductory to advanced in monthly, two-month (bimestral) or four-month (cuatrimestral) formats, plus thematic workshops; there are also special tracks for Portuguese-speaking (Brazilian) students.

The only requirement is to be over 16. Enrolment is online through a step-by-step guide before each term; fees are published on the 'Aranceles de Español' page. Buenos Aires is a popular, relatively affordable city for Spanish immersion, and UBA certificates are widely recognised in the region.

UBC Future Global Leaders is the University of British Columbia's pre-university programme for teenagers. Students take university-style courses in areas such as business, science, engineering, psychology and global issues, taught by UBC instructors, and get a taste of campus life at one of Canada's top universities.

The on-campus programme runs in July and August at UBC Vancouver, with online courses also offered in the summer. It is open to students aged 15–18 who have completed grade 10 or equivalent; there is no application, transcript or English test, only registration, though English-language learners must meet the published English thresholds. 2027 course dates and fees will be posted on the UBC Extended Learning page.

UC Berkeley Summer Sessions offers hundreds of regular Berkeley courses to visiting students, including a dedicated 'Visiting International' pathway with visa information, an English proficiency requirement and an international checklist. Students choose among sessions of different lengths and earn UC Berkeley credit that can transfer to their home university.

In 2026 sessions ran from 26 May to 14 August (Sessions A–F and a 12-week session); 2027 should follow a similar pattern. Applications open in February; check the Session Dates & Deadlines and Tuition and Fees pages for 2027 details.

ucl-summer-school-2027.about:
Every July and August UCL, one of the world's top-ranked universities, runs a summer school in Bloomsbury, central London, for students from universities worldwide (in 2026, from 50 countries and over 250 universities). Students choose from 50+ undergraduate modules developed by UCL academics for credit and taught face to face, studying one module per three-week session or two modules across both sessions (six weeks); many modules use London itself through excursions.

The programme is for students who have completed at least one year of undergraduate study (second- and third-year students and graduates are common; some postgraduates and professionals). Participants are guaranteed discounted UCL accommodation and can join an evening and weekend social and cultural programme. Apply before 1 March 2027 to avoid the GBP 60 application fee.

The International Summer School of the Universidad de los Andes School of Management (one of Latin America's top business schools) brings international professors to Bogotá each June and July. unitartu-summer-school-2027.about:
UniTartu Summer School brings students and lifelong learners to the University of Tartu for English-taught courses, mostly in the compact student city of Tartu. In 2026 it offered 13 courses in science and technology (for example synthetic biology and self-driving cars), social sciences (such as disinformation) and the arts and humanities, each lasting one or two weeks, plus a social and cultural programme exploring Estonia.

The 2027 edition runs 2–13 August 2027, with courses added through the autumn and the full list by early January 2027. Each application costs a non-refundable EUR 25 (covering up to two programmes); course fees are listed on each course page. Sign up for the newsletter to hear about the application period and early-bird discount.
highlights: English-taught courses in tech, social sciences and humanities
One- or two-week formats in a student city
Low EUR 25 application fee; early-bird discount
unitartu-summer-school-2027.eligibility: University students and lifelong learners; each course lists its own admission requirements. All nationalities.
how_to_apply: Check the UniTartu Summer School page from early January 2027 for the course list
Choose up to two courses and check their requirements and fees
Apply in the application period and pay the EUR 25 application fee by the deadline
Pay the course fee after admission
unitartu-summer-school-2027.costs: Application fee EUR 25 (non-refundable, covers up to two programmes); course fees vary by course; optional cultural events extra.

united-hacks-v8-2027.about:
United Hacks is a recurring online hackathon organised by Hack United, a student-led nonprofit. In V8, participants build a brand-new project over one weekend in either the General track (any topic, from accessibility to mental health) or the Theme track, whose theme is announced at the opening ceremony on 8 January 2027 at 7:00 pm EST.

Submissions (public repository, 2–5 minute demo video and written description) are due on 10 January at noon EST, followed by a closing ceremony. Prizes include cash for 1st/2nd in each track, best solo hack, best pitch and participant prizes; workshops and communication run through Discord.
highlights: General and theme tracks
Cash, gadget and sponsor prizes
Workshops and team-finding on Discord
united-hacks-v8-2027.eligibility: Students (typically high school and university) worldwide; check the Devpost rules for exact age limits. One team per participant; code must be written during the event.
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

university-of-ghana-ghana-to-the-world-s.about:
Ghana to the World is the University of Ghana's international summer school, run by its International Programmes Office on the Legon campus in Accra. Participants attend interactive lectures on Africa-centred topics, can study for academic credit, take part in cultural activities, tour several regions of Ghana and volunteer in disadvantaged communities.

The programme typically runs a June cohort and a late-summer (August–September) cohort, and can be arranged for groups at other times. The programme fee is USD 3,000 per person; participants are self-funded or sponsored by their institutions. Apply through the IPO's online form and contact iposummerschools@ug.edu.gh for 2027 dates.
highlights: Lectures at Ghana's oldest and largest university
Regional tours and community volunteering
Option to earn academic credit
university-of-ghana-ghana-to-the-world-s.eligibility: Students (mainly university level) and groups from any country; confirm specific requirements with the International Programmes Office.
how_to_apply: Request information or apply through the IPO 'Apply Now' form
Choose the June or late-summer cohort
Arrange funding (self or institutional) for the USD 3,000 fee
Apply for a Ghanaian visa and required vaccinations (yellow fever)
university-of-ghana-ghana-to-the-world-s.costs: Programme fee USD 3,000 per person; flights and visa extra.

uoft-international-english-program-2027.about:
The International English Program (IEP) at the University of Toronto's New College is a summer English programme for adults (18+) of all levels, ideal for university students or graduates preparing to study in English. Morning courses are General English, Academic English or Culture & Community (15 hours per week); afternoon electives include Words in Motion and Discuss to Debate.

2027 sessions run 5–23 July and 26 July–13 August. Each course costs CAD 1,950, plus a CAD 200 registration fee and CAD 160 health insurance; optional residence costs CAD 1,260 per session and meal plans CAD 260–880. A typical package with residence and two meals a day is about CAD 4,405. Final payment is due 6 June (July) or 27 June (August) 2027, and fees are refunded (minus non-refundable fees) if a Canadian visa is refused.
highlights: Academic English option for future university study
Flexible: course only or with residence and meals
Refund if the Canadian visa is refused
uoft-international-english-program-2027.eligibility: Adults aged 18 or older of any nationality and English level.
how_to_apply: Choose a session and morning/afternoon courses
Apply online through U of T International Programs
Pay the registration fee and arrange residence if wanted
Apply for a Canadian visa or eTA
Pay the balance by 6 June or 27 June 2027
uoft-international-english-program-2027.costs: Course CAD 1,950 + registration CAD 200 + insurance CAD 160; optional residence CAD 1,260 and meals CAD 260–880 per 3-week session.

uoft-national-biology-competition-2027.about:
The National Biology Competition (NBC) is an annual online biology exam organised by the University of Toronto for secondary-school students. Students answer multiple-choice questions covering high-school and early-university biology, supervised at their own school; top students and schools receive certificates and prizes, and the competition is a good benchmark for biology olympiad preparation.

In 2026 seats could be purchased from 2 March to 6 April, student registration closed 7 April and the exam ran 8–9 April; 2027 is expected to follow the same April timing. The fee is CAD 7 per student (minimum five students per school), and the exam is offered in English only. Schools outside Canada can enter: the top three schools outside Canada receive a Certificate of Excellence.
highlights: Run by the University of Toronto
Very low cost: CAD 7 per student
Schools outside Canada ranked separately
uoft-national-biology-competition-2027.eligibility: Students in grades 9–12 registered through a secondary school (minimum 5 students per school), in Canada or abroad. English only.
how_to_apply: Ask a biology teacher to register the school and buy seats (March)
Register each student before the deadline
Write the online exam at school on the April test day under supervision
uoft-national-biology-competition-2027.costs: CAD 7 per student, minimum 5 students per school.

uoft-pre-university-program-2027.about:
The Pre-University Program is run by New College's International Programs at the University of Toronto, Canada's top-ranked university. High-school students with advanced English take one morning and one afternoon course in university-style subjects, live in a supervised residence on the downtown St. George campus, and join evening activities and weekend excursions around Toronto.

In 2027 there are three three-week sessions: 13 June–3 July, 4 July–24 July and 25 July–14 August. The international all-inclusive fee is CAD 6,625 (classes, residence, all meals, supervision, activities, excursions, health insurance and airport transfers); a CAD 600 non-refundable deposit holds a place. Students who need a visa should apply well before the final-payment deadlines (16 May, 6 June and 27 June 2027 by session).
highlights: Two university-style courses on the U of T St. George campus
All-inclusive: residence, meals, insurance, excursions
Three session dates across the summer
uoft-pre-university-program-2027.eligibility: High-school students aged 15–18 from any country with advanced English. International students may need a Canadian visitor visa.
how_to_apply: Choose a session and two courses on the Pre-University Program page
Complete the online application through International Programs
Pay the CAD 600 deposit to hold a place
Apply for a Canadian visa if needed
Pay the balance by the session's final-payment deadline
uoft-pre-university-program-2027.costs: International all-inclusive fee CAD 6,625 for three weeks (Canadian citizens/PR CAD 4,995). CAD 600 deposit non-refundable. Flights extra.

uoft-youth-international-english-program.about:
The Youth International English Program (Youth IEP) is a residential English-language summer camp run by New College at the University of Toronto. Students of all English levels take a morning course (General English for ages 13–18, or IELTS Preparation and Academic Preparation for ages 15–18) and can add afternoon courses such as Read, Write & Remix, Culture & Community or Global Commerce.

Sessions run 13 June–3 July, 4–24 July and 25 July–14 August 2027. Fees are all-inclusive: CAD 5,725 for General English and CAD 5,925 for IELTS or Academic Preparation, covering classes, residence, meals, insurance, supervision, airport transfers, evening events and weekend trips; optional afternoon courses cost CAD 700 each. A full refund (minus the CAD 500 deposit) is given if a Canadian visa is refused.
highlights: IELTS preparation option for ages 15–18
All-inclusive residence, meals, insurance and trips
Refund if the Canadian visa is refused
uoft-youth-international-english-program.eligibility: Students aged 13–18 of any nationality and any English level (IELTS and Academic Preparation courses: ages 15–18).
how_to_apply: Choose a session and morning course
Apply online through U of T International Programs
Pay the CAD 500 deposit
Apply for a Canadian visa if needed
Pay the balance by the final-payment deadline for your session
uoft-youth-international-english-program.costs: CAD 5,725 (General English) or CAD 5,925 (IELTS / Academic Preparation) all-inclusive for three weeks; optional afternoon courses CAD 700 each; CAD 500 deposit non-refundable.
